 The Cincinnati Bengals will host the Tennessee Titans while the Cleveland Browns will head to Pittsburgh to take on the Steelers at 1 p.m. on Sunday, Nov. 1.
 Cincinnati (4-2) is looking to pick up a third straight win before the Bengals head to Madrid, Spain to face Atlanta in an international game next week. The game against Tennessee (1-6) will be televised on CBS.
 Cincinnati Bengals: Offense found success with Burrow back in shotgun Cleveland (5-2) is also looking for a third straight victory and to hold onto the team’s lead in the AFC North with a matchup against the rival Steelers (5-2). The Browns have not won a regular-season game in Pittsburgh since Oct. 5, 2003.
 Cleveland fans will need the Sunday Ticket to view that game.
 In other NFL matchups Thursday Night Football will feature Carolina (3-3) at Green Bay (4-3) at 8:15 p.m. on Prime Video.
 On Sunday the FOX single game will be Minnesota (6-0) at Detroit (4-2) at 1 p.m., the CBS late game will have Kansas City (5-1) at Denver (5-2) at 4:25 p.m. and the Sunday Night Football game is Philadelphia (2-5) at Washington (1-4-1) at 8:20 p.m. on NBC.
 Monday Night Football will wrap up the week with Chicago (5-2) at Seattle (4-3) at 8:15 p.m. on ESPN.
